items.note: Single-group classroom ideation exercise in which every participant received an AI-generated image stimulus; evaluators rated the 18 best ideas and traced their inspiration source, so there is no comparison condition (all participants had the AI stimulus).

ICIS short paper describing an experimental series in which people develop ideas with generative-AI feedback, manipulating numeric versus visual feedback and its timing (AI configuration versus AI configuration); may be a design proposal with no results yet, N not stated; related to the Gordetzki et al. ISR paper.

Experiment with three sequential creativity tasks finding AI use raises creative performance but biases estimates of one's own and others' creativity, with a one-week follow-up; AOM proceedings abstract, N and assignment not stated.

180 participants brainstormed solutions with AI assistants holding different values (AI configuration versus AI configuration, no no-AI arm); ideas were coded for the AI's values, but idea quality is only self-evaluated, so a creativity or diversity outcome on output is uncertain; arXiv 2402.12814 is the same work.

System paper (MetaEmbody) with a user study of 20 designers reporting higher novelty and feasibility ratings than a comparison condition; unclear whether ratings are by experts or self-reports; below 50 participants.

Online experiment with 298 participants who ideated after viewing DALL-E 2 art, traditional art, or no art; originality and number of ideas scored; AI output used as a stimulus rather than an interactive assistant.

Classroom 6-3-5 ideation workshop in which student groups could use ChatGPT, Google, or no support; novelty of concepts analyzed, AI ideas more novel; assignment to groups described as 'advised', N not stated.

Lab experiment with 60 two-person teams (120 students) assigned to unequal, full, or no GenAI access writing a press release; task quality graded (search notes say professionals also rated originality and that assignment was random); ASIS&T 2025 short paper 10.1002/pra2.1437 is the same study.

System paper (POET) that diversifies text-to-image outputs; evaluation with 28 users across four creative domains reports higher perceived diversity and fewer prompts, comparison condition not described in the abstract; arXiv 2504.13392 is the same work; below 50 participants.

Field experiment with nearly 100 Egyptian senior students: treatment wrote three graded essays with ChatGPT, control without, then both played an unaided lab innovation game where the ChatGPT group scored 0.6-0.72 SD lower (after_ai); assignment method not stated; bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2024.04.03.588037 is the same study.
